title: Leakage-Aware Authenticated Encryption for Encode-then-Encipher
summary: Encode-then-encipher is secure against release of unverified plaintext, but extending the leakage-aware authenticated-encryption framework to this setting remains open.

formal_statement.body: Extend the leakage-aware authenticated-encryption framework to encode-then-encipher constructions. A MAC-then-encrypt construction becomes a form of encode-then-encipher when its encryption component $E$ is a tweakable variable-input-length cipher, and encode-then-encipher is secure against release of unverified plaintext. The unresolved task is to formulate and prove the extension in the presence of leakage; no particular generic-composition theorem or sufficient conditions on $E$ are specified as requirements for this extension.

scope.domain: Leakage-aware authenticated encryption for encode-then-encipher constructions.
parameters: E: the encryption component of the MAC-then-encrypt construction, described as a tweakable variable-input-length cipher
scope.unresolved_remainder: Formulate and prove an extension of the leakage-aware authenticated-encryption framework to the encode-then-encipher setting.

citations.label: Authenticated Encryption in the Face of Protocol and Side Channel Leakage

progress.summary: The source motivates the setting through its security against release of unverified plaintext and explicitly leaves extension of the leakage-aware framework open. It presents this separately from the question of sufficient conditions for generic composition under leakage.
citation_labels: Guy Barwell et al., Authenticated Encryption in the Face of Protocol and Side Channel Leakage
